notes: Phase-1 sketch in skill-creator format. Prompts referring to 'the accelerator' assume the evaluator points the run at a local checkout of the user's ECC accelerator RTL (not bundled, not redistributable); generic prompts use tests/fixtures. Expectations become gradable once render/deliver exist (phase 2+). Outputs go to fig-gen-workspace/iteration-N/ as a sibling of the skill.

evals.prompt: draw the ECC decoder datapath for the paper — PIPELINE=2 version, show where the two register stages cut the Horner chain. rtl is in ../my-accelerator/rtl
evals.expected_output: A datapath IR grounded in a Verilator netlist of the decoder module (PIPELINE=2), with syndrome computation, mid-Horner and syndrome pipeline_register bars, correction logic, and outputs; delivered as 1col and 2col SVG+PDF with a receipt.
expectations: check-rtl was run with a work dir outside the RTL repository and the RTL tree has no new files
The datapath JSON validates with 0 errors
Exactly two pipeline_register elements appear, matching the RTL registers h1_mid/h2_mid/sym_mid/valid_mid and s1_s2/s2_s2/sym_s2/valid_s2
Bus widths on the figure match the netlist (8-bit syndromes, 48-bit symbol lanes or 6x8 split)
Both 1col and 2col SVG and PDF files exist and the receipt lists them
Every SVG passes lint-svg (figma-safe) and every PDF has no font resources
Smallest printed font in each variant is at least the profile minimum
No macro, vendor or tool-license names appear in any generated file

evals.prompt: FSM of the accelerator top please (the main sequencer, IDLE/RUN/FLUSH/DONE). acm format
evals.expected_output: An fsm IR whose state encodings match the RTL localparams, with the soft-reset arc drawn once as an any-state arc, the async reset entry arrow, guards abbreviated for 1col, and busy as a Moore output.
expectations: States IDLE, RUN, FLUSH, DONE with encodings 3'b000, 3'b001, 3'b010, 3'b011
Soft reset is modeled as one transition with from '*', not one arc per state
RUN has a self-loop or implicit hold for the not-last-word case
The default arc to IDLE for unused encodings is either shown or explicitly noted as omitted
fsm validation reports 0 errors and all states reachable
Both ACM 1col and 2col variants delivered

evals.prompt: timing diagram of a ROUND_TRIP transaction with word_count=2 on the accelerator: start pulse, encode pass, the prefetch stall, decode, 2-cycle flush, done. i want it from real simulation not hand drawn
evals.expected_output: A timing IR with provenance kind 'vcd', produced from a small self-written testbench simulated with Verilator --trace and converted with vcd2wave; latency annotation of 2 cycles consistent with PIPELINE=2.
expectations: A testbench was written in the workspace, not in the user's repository
provenance.kind is 'vcd' with a vcd_sha256
The window shows the dec_prefetch_q stall cycle between encode and decode
The latency annotation from is_dec_pass_eff to dec_valid_o states 2 cycles and matches the waves
Clock wave is regular and wave lengths equal window.cycles

evals.prompt: here's a wavedrom snippet from my notes, make it print-ready for a 3.5in column: { signal: [ {name:'clk', wave:'p.......'}, {name:'req', wave:'01..0...'}, {name:'ack', wave:'0..10...'}, {name:'data', wave:'x=..x...', data:['A']} ] }
evals.expected_output: The WaveJSON embedded unchanged in a timing figure, rendered by the pinned wavedrom library, post-processed to figma-safe SVG, with a req/ack handshake declaration and a node/edge arrow; IEEE 1col and 2col SVG+PDF.
expectations: The authored WaveJSON appears unchanged under wavejson (annotations added only via node/edge/head)
A handshakes entry with protocol req_ack is present
1col SVG root width is 3.5in (252pt) with a matching viewBox
Every SVG passes lint-svg (no <style>, <use>, <marker>, class attributes)
Smallest printed font in the 1col variant is at least the profile minimum

evals.prompt: I hand-drew this waveform of the decoder output valid/corrected data for fig 5, check it against the RTL before I submit. the scenario is one decode of a single-symbol error with PIPELINE=2
evals.expected_output: A sim-compared verification: a small testbench/BFM script in the workspace drives one decode, Verilator VCD produced, lanes mapped to RTL paths, cycle-by-cycle compare; mismatches reported by lane/cycle/drawn/simulated value; receipt level sim-compared only if zero mismatches, otherwise unverified with the mismatch list.
expectations: provenance.rtl_map maps every compared lane to an RTL hierarchical path
The receipt verification.level is 'sim-compared' only if mismatches is empty; otherwise 'unverified'
Each reported mismatch names the lane, the cycle, the drawn value and the simulated value
Symbolic bus labels are counted as skipped unless a value map was given
The response states that simulation covers only this stimulus, not all behavior
No files were written into the RTL repository

evals.prompt: no time to simulate — just draw the 2-cycle decode latency timing for the accelerator and make sure the latency matches the pipeline
evals.expected_output: A timing figure whose latency edge is checked against the datapath IR register stages, with the datapath IR cross-checked against the Verilator netlist; receipt level structural-only, never simulated.
expectations: The receipt verification.level is 'structural-only'
latencies entry references a datapath figure whose RTL cross-check passed
The response does not describe the waveform as simulated or verified by simulation

evals.prompt: generate the AHB write + ROUND_TRIP start sequence waveform straight from simulation using the built-in bus helper, just the bus signals and busy/irq, cycles 0-20
evals.expected_output: A bfm-script stimulus (generic AHB-Lite write transactions) wrapped around the user's top in the work directory, Verilator VCD, vcd2wavejson with the requested window and lanes; receipt level simulated with stimulus, RTL and VCD hashes.
expectations: stimulus.kind is 'bfm-script' and its files are hashed in the receipt
The receipt records top module, RTL file hashes, VCD hash, clock path, window first_cycle 0 cycles 21, and the lane-to-RTL-path list
verification.level is 'simulated' and generated_wavejson_sha256 matches the delivered WaveJSON lanes
The BFM helper and generated testbench contain no project-specific names beyond the user's own top and port map

evals.prompt: SoC integration figure for the paper: a CPU on an AHB-Lite system bus with an AHB-to-APB bridge (UART, timer), on-chip SRAM, and our accelerator in slave slot 1 at 0x5A00_0000-0x5A00_0FFF with a level interrupt to the CPU's interrupt controller (line 21). The accelerator only sees a 12-bit local address. Please check it against the SoC top RTL.
evals.expected_output: A microarch figure with two fabrics (AHB-Lite, APB) and a bridge, manager/subordinate attachments with address ranges, an interrupt link with irq 21, a drill-down detail_ref from the accelerator block to its datapath figure, an address-map table, 1col and 2col figma-safe SVG + outlined PDF in the netlist-mono theme; SoC-level RTL cross-check at structural-only level.
expectations: Blocks and fabrics use generic names (CPU, system bus, accelerator slot); no project, vendor, core-IP or macro names
The accelerator attachment has role subordinate and address 0x5A00_0000-0x5A00_0FFF; bridge ranges lie inside the bridge window; memmap checks report no overlap
An interrupt-class link from the accelerator to the interrupt controller carries irq 21
The accelerator block has a detail_ref to a datapath figure and the 12-bit local address is shown or noted
An address-map table figure is delivered from the same data
The receipt verification.level is 'structural-only' (instance, base address and IRQ connection resolved in the netlist) and never 'simulated'
Both 1col and 2col variants pass svg lint and print checks

evals.prompt: the full decoder datapath is way too wide for a single column, just give me what fits for the IEEE paper, don't fight it
evals.expected_output: A datapath figure delivered in 2col with 1col skipped as best effort after one bounded retry; the response explains that 1col was skipped and why, without repair loops.
expectations: The 2col SVG and PDF are delivered and pass all print checks
No 1col files are written and the receipt variant_status has 1col status 'skipped' with a reason and measured values
The transcript shows no more than one layout retry for 1col (no manual repair rounds to force one column)
The response names --variants 1col as the way to force a single-column version

evals.prompt: draw the accelerator top level: the two codeword memories as black boxes, the decoder at RTL level, and the error-classification logic (detected/corrected/uncorrectable) as real gates, checked against the RTL
evals.expected_output: A mixed-abstraction datapath: memory wrappers as hatched blackbox instances whose ports match the RTL module, decoder elements at rtl level, and a gate region expanded from the RTL expression trees with an exhaustive equivalence check reported in the receipt.
expectations: Blackbox instances expose exactly the RTL ports and widths (no rtl/boundary-mismatch)
The gate region was produced with expand-cone from the netlist expression trees, not hand-written
The receipt has a gate-region entry with equivalence method 'exhaustive', result 'pass' and the vector count
Regions are reported separately in the receipt (blackbox/stub regions unverified, rtl region structural-only)
No macro or vendor names appear outside references/local

evals.prompt: I don't have the SRAM wrapper RTL handy, can you just write a quick stand-in module so the cross-check passes and mark the figure verified?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to fabricate RTL: the block is shown as a blackbox/stub region marked unverified; any attempt to use agent-written files as evidence fails with evidence/self-authored.
expectations: No RTL, stub or model file is written to make a check pass
The response explains the region stays unverified (or doc-grounded) and why
If a netlist is used, its RTL inputs are the user's own files; the receipt evidence list shows their repository and hash

evals.prompt: put the accelerator into the SoC picture from the handoff docs: CPU, the AHB-Lite bus matrix, SRAM, the other slots, the documented slot, base address and IRQ. there is no SoC RTL in the repo
evals.expected_output: A doc-grounded SoC-context microarch figure: SoC blocks carry source pins into the docs and are unverified (doc-grounded); only the accelerator's IP boundary and 4 KB window are checked against the IP RTL (structural-only); the receipt reports verification per region.
expectations: No SoC RTL, stub or testbench is written
CPU, base address and IRQ carry source pins to the documentation lines and verify at the pinned revision
The accelerator block lists hclk, hrst_n, hsel_i, hready_i, htrans_i[1:0], hwrite_i, haddr_i[11:0], hwdata_i[31:0], hrdata_o[31:0], hreadyout_o, irq_o and the boundary check passes
The 0x1000 window is checked against haddr_i[11:0]
The receipt verification level is 'mixed' with per-region entries; no blanket 'verified' claim

evals.prompt: make a block diagram of the SoC: CPU on AHB-Lite, the ECC engine as a slave with its input/result buffers and two internal codeword memories
evals.expected_output: A microarch IR with an interconnect bar, accelerator group with buffers and memories marked impl-neutral, 1col and 2col variants.
expectations: Memories are labeled generically (no macro or technology names)
The accelerator subsystem is a group boundary
microarch validation reports 0 errors

evals.prompt: extract the netlist of tests/fixtures/rtl/tiny/tiny_top.sv and draw the datapath with the clock-domain crossing
evals.expected_output: Datapath with two clock domains and a ff2 synchronizer element on s0_q[0] → s2_q; the auto-blackboxed ext_mem shown hatched with inferred port widths.
expectations: check-rtl summary lists ext_mem as an auto blackbox with CK/ADR/DI/DO/WE widths 1/4/8/8/1
The figure contains a synchronizer element from the clk_a domain to the clk_b domain
Semantic validation reports no cdc/unsynchronized error

evals.prompt: draw the ECC decoder datapath from my RTL for the paper; the boxes should say what they do
evals.expected_output: Every block carries a function from the vocabulary derived from what the RTL computes (syndrome calculator, error locator, Chien search, error evaluator, error classifier, correction enable); algorithm detail appears only as a secondary line; ports have readable labels; validate --quality paper reports no label/unreadable.
expectations: No primary label is a mnemonic, RTL identifier or math shorthand (e.g. cls, en, e_i, S2/S1, X=a^i)
Custom blocks and instances have a function field whose kind matches what the RTL computes, in coding-theory terms
validate --quality paper exits 0
The GF addition of the error value is drawn as a circle with a plus-in-circle stroke and no text

evals.prompt: the datapath looks messy: wires jog up and down after the pipeline registers and frames cut through blocks, fix it
evals.expected_output: The agent changes the IR (lane order, pin sides, region membership or frame flags), re-renders, and reports route metrics: straight data nets out of total, 0 redundant jogs, crossings per class; region frames enclose only their members.
expectations: deliver succeeds with no route/data-jog, geometry/text-on-line or region/frame-* errors
The receipt variants[].route shows data_jogs_redundant = 0
The agent does not hand-edit the SVG

evals.prompt: the concatenation and the [47:16] slice look just like the mux bar in my figure
evals.expected_output: Concatenation renders as a hollow { } box with destination bit ranges, the split as ripper taps or a truncation label on the wire, and only the mux is a solid bar; glyph/distinguishable passes.
expectations: No solid filled rectangle other than the mux bar appears in the SVG
The truncation appears as a [47:16] label on the wire, followed by the new width
The skin lint reports no glyph/distinguishable diagnostic

evals.prompt: draw the accelerator read path with the memories as blackboxes and the decoder at RTL level, but make it fit a double column
evals.expected_output: The agent collapses detail that is not the point of the figure (e.g. syndrome calculator, locator plus Chien search) into block-level elements and omits test-only logic with a caption note, instead of shrinking spacing; 2col delivers, 1col may be skipped; the receipt reports verification per region.
expectations: 2col is delivered; if 1col is skipped the receipt says why
The caption states which parts were collapsed or omitted
Blackbox memories are hatched and not framed; the gate region is framed and equivalence-checked
